**Formulating activity estimates**

I'm looking at the activities and need to sum up the estimates. I should distinguish between the U3 exploratory repository options and decide on a prototype, which I think might take about 40 hours. For the U6 messaging expression, it's likely to be around 80 hours. I see that module moves are involved, so I'll make sure to factor those in. Let’s get this organized!

technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing Spring XD/Spring Cloud Data Flow module registry and module metadata conventions rather than introducing a new registry mechanism.
Implement the HDFS sink using the Hadoop filesystem client API and preserve the existing sink module lifecycle, configuration, and message-handling patterns.
Implement Hadoop shell commands through the existing shell command extension mechanism, with command services isolated from end-to-end stream deployment.

Use a repository abstraction for composed-job definitions so storage can be backed by the existing supported repository technology without coupling orchestration logic to a specific persistence implementation.
Represent composed jobs as declarative definitions referencing existing jobs and their parameters, with orchestration delegated to the existing job and stream execution services where possible.
Implement module message binding using the framework's existing message headers, payload expressions, and property resolution facilities rather than creating a separate expression language.

Move JDBC and Kafka modules with their existing public configuration semantics where practical, adapting package names, build metadata, module descriptors, and compatibility APIs to the target repository.
Favor backward-compatible APIs and configuration properties; add adapters only where the source and target repository contracts differ.
Use unit and component tests for command handling, module binding, repository operations, orchestration, and moved modules, with a limited number of end-to-end smoke tests.
assumptions: The existing repositories, build system, module framework, shell framework, job infrastructure, and test conventions are available and buildable by the developer.
The referenced external document for U5 is unavailable; the estimate assumes isolation tests for command parsing, validation, service invocation, success responses, and error handling.

The increment requires implementation and automated tests but not production deployment, operational support, performance benchmarking, security certification, or migration of an existing production data store.
Hadoop and Kafka dependencies can be added or aligned with versions already supported by the project; no major upstream library rewrite is required.
HDFS authentication is limited to the existing supported Hadoop configuration and credentials model; Kerberos-specific discovery and infrastructure setup are excluded.
The composed-job repository will initially support the repository technology already used by the project and will provide a clean abstraction for future storage options.
Composed-job orchestration reuses existing scheduling, launching, status, and error-reporting facilities and does not introduce a new distributed workflow engine.
The JDBC and Kafka moves are source-level module migrations with compatibility verification, not complete redesigns of those modules.
One developer performs implementation, tests, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work-hours and include normal code review preparation but not waiting time for external reviews.
Requirements are sufficiently stable during implementation; substantial changes to composed-job semantics or module binding semantics would require a re-estimate.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module registry, shell command framework, job and stream execution services, repository abstractions, message binding conventions, build layout, and existing test infrastructure. Map each user story to affected components and identify compatibility constraints.

Create or update module projects, build descriptors, dependency versions, profiles, configuration templates, and local development fixtures required for Hadoop, Kafka, JDBC, expression evaluation, and repository/orchestration work.

activities.activity_name: HDFS sink and module registry integration
activities.activity_description: Implement the HDFS sink module, including message-to-file writing behavior, path and file configuration, resource handling, error propagation, module metadata, registry registration, and unit/component tests.

Add shell commands for querying and interacting with the Hadoop file system through the existing shell extension model. Implement command parsing, option validation, Hadoop client invocation, output formatting, error handling, help text, and command-level tests.

Evaluate viable repository options, document the trade-offs, define the composed-job persistence model and repository interface, implement the selected repository adapter, and add serialization, validation, CRUD, and repository integration tests.

Implement composed-job definition validation, dependency and execution ordering, job launch coordination, parameter propagation, status tracking, failure handling, restart or completion behavior consistent with existing capabilities, command/API integration, and orchestration tests.

Refactor shell command dependencies where necessary to permit isolated testing, add mocks and test fixtures, cover valid and invalid inputs, command output, Hadoop/client failures, authorization failures, and regression cases without deploying a complete stream.

Define supported binding expressions and precedence rules, implement payload/header/property resolution, integrate binding into module invocation, handle missing or invalid properties, preserve existing binding behavior, and add unit and component coverage across representative modules.

Move the JDBC sink module into the target Spring Cloud Stream repository, adapt package and build metadata, align configuration and binding contracts, preserve sink behavior, update documentation and descriptors, and run compatibility and integration tests.

Move the Kafka source module into the target repository, adapt dependencies, package structure, configuration, module descriptors, and binding contracts, preserve source behavior, update documentation, and run broker-backed or equivalent integration tests.

Execute the complete build and test matrix, add integration coverage for registry discovery, HDFS sink usage, Hadoop shell interaction, composed-job persistence and orchestration, expression binding, and migrated JDBC/Kafka modules; fix cross-feature defects and compatibility regressions.

Document configuration, shell commands, composed-job definitions and lifecycle, expression binding syntax, migrated module usage, Hadoop prerequisites, upgrade considerations, and known limitations. Clean up diagnostics, configuration defaults, and release artifacts.
